subject: NDX discovery: model fit recs + user-query sample intake
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@ndx-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ndx-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo recap (NDX)

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier — that was helpful. A couple quick clarifications for internal folks at NDX: 1) Our primary use case is customer support triage where we summarize multi-turn chat transcripts and suggest next actions; 2) We have a hard constraint that any model pipeline must support on-prem or VPC private deployment for regulated customers; 3) Latency SLO for generate path is ~250ms tail for short prompts (<=128 tokens).

Samir will attach an initial CSV with ~150 anonymized user queries (we've redacted direct PII but left medical/financial topic hints). We'll need Redwood's recommendations on model family, quantization tradeoffs, and a suggested prompt set for evaluation. Also: can you flag any obvious quality-regression risks we should watch for?

Best,
Elena
Director, Product
NDX Analytics
[Attachment: ndx_user_queries_sample.csv (csv, 42KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@ndx-analytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@ndx-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo recap (NDX)

Hi Elena — great to meet you both; thanks for sending the sample. Samir — received the CSV, thanks. Quick responses inline: 

- Model family: for NDX's triage/summarization + next-action suggestions we recommend trying rw-infer-14b-q4f for best quality/cost balance and rw-infer-7b-int8 for a lower-cost baseline. For embeddings (search/semantic match) start with rw-embed-2.7b.
- Deployment: both recommended variants are available for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and we can provide a verification checklist for your infra team.
- Latency: 250ms tail for <=128 tokens will be tight at 14B in single-shot mode without batching; we'll propose batching/caching strategies and an autoscaling baseline in the follow-up doc.
- Quality risks: multi-turn context truncation (you mentioned long transcripts), hallucination on entity normalization (names/IDs), and safety/sensitive-topic handling in medical/financial prompts. We should include targeted evals for those.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ben/Marissa and I will map a small eval plan (5 canonical prompts + 12 edge cases) and share a short runbook for redaction.
2) Please confirm where you'll upload the full 150-query CSV (Drive link or S3). If you can't share raw user text, a version with tokenized context or hashed IDs will work for early model-fit checks.
3) We'll run a quick benchmark and return: model recommendations, latency/cost estimates, and a short sample of failure modes within 3 business days.

Attaching our redaction examples so you can compare against your CSV.

Thanks — Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redaction_examples_per_policy.txt (txt, 3KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ndx-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Novak <elena.novak@ndx-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo recap (NDX)

Thanks Neha — uploading full set to a temporary S3 bucket as you requested. Link below (expires in 7 days). We redacted direct PII (emails, phone numbers) but left topic flags ("billing", "prescription", etc.). We also included a small folder "edge_cases" with ~18 transcripts that are longer or contain shorthand and non-standard punctuation.

S3 (temp): https://s3.amazonaws.com/ndx-redwood-samples/ndx-150-v1.csv
Edge cases folder: https://s3.amazonaws.com/ndx-redwood-samples/edge_cases/

Attachments: ndx_security_requirements.pdf (security questionnaire; high level)

—Samir

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ndx-analytics.com>, Elena Novak <elena.novak@ndx-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo recap (NDX)

Perfect — thanks for the upload and the edge-case folder, Samir. We pulled a quick sample and started a two-track plan (low-effort smoke run + deeper eval):

A) Smoke run (24–48 hours):
- Models: rw-infer-7b-int8 and rw-infer-14b-q4f
- Tests: 50 random queries + 10 edge transcripts (from your edge_cases) for summarization quality, hallucination check, and action-suggestion correctness.
- Deliverable: short report with per-model PSNR-style quality scores (precision/recall on suggested actions), latency summary, and 3-5 example failure traces.

B) Deeper eval (5 business days):
- Build prompt set: canonical prompts (5) + 12 targeted edge cases focusing on context truncation, entity normalization, and ambiguous user intents. We'll use your edge_cases examples as seeds.
- Redaction guidance: follow the linked playbook; we recommend replacing direct identifiers with stable tokens (e.g., [USER_ID_#]) and keeping the topic hint (medical/finance) as free text. We'll also run a sensitive-topics safety classifier to flag outputs that require human review.
- Benchmarks & links: see our internal benchmark sheet and the redaction playbook (links below).

Immediate action items: 
- Samir/Elena: confirm S3 expiry date and grant redwood-demo@redwood.ai read access (we already validated the link works).
- Ben: can you lead the procurement touchpoint if we need a short-term Dedicated slot for the smoke run? I'll include Jonas on the capacity questions.
- Marissa: I'll draft the prompt set and share a Google Doc for your review by EOD tomorrow.

Links:
- Benchmarks: https://drive.redwood.ai/ndx/benchmarks/ndx-smoke-2026-11
- Redaction playbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/redaction-playbook
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/NDX-2026-04

If that plan looks good I'll queue the smoke run first thing tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ndx_security_requirements.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]
